newsitem.title: ITALY: STET merger seen boosting shares but worry lingers.
newsitem.headline: STET merger seen boosting shares but worry lingers.

text.p: The impending mega merger of two of Italy's largest telecoms companies looks set to drive the joint group's share price higher, but some analysts said on Thursday they were worried the hype may be clouding more fundamental concerns.

Italy's state-controlled telecoms holding group STET will absorb its operating company Telecom Italia on Friday and the combined group, to be known as Telecom Italia SpA , will start trading on the Milan bourse on Monday.

The merger is seen as sweeping away the complex structure of Italy's telecoms industry, putting the new Telecom Italia on the same footing as many of its European counterparts and paving the way for its privatisation later this year.
Both shares risen due to potential merger benefits and a number a strategic link-ups announced recently.
"The pieces of the puzzle are falling nicely into place, and the share price is fully justified,", said Evan Miller telecoms industry analyst at broker CS First Boston.

He sees a price target for the new Telecom Italia shares of 13,300 lire ($7.63), possibly as soon as the end of this year, while analyst Philip Townsend at brokers Smith Barney sees a share valuation range of 12,000 to 15,000 lire.
STET shares were up 5.47 percent at 11,610 lire and Telecom Italia 5.61-percent higher at 6,435 lire by 1335 GMT.

"The positives for the share price are the internal growth potential in Italy, cost cutting, the link up with a well-known name like AT&T and potential growth from its mobile phone business TIM (Telecom Italia Mobile)," said Townsend.
The new Telecom Italia will have a controlling stake in Europe's largest cellular phone company, TIM , which has shown high growth rates recently.
But some analysts worry over STET's reputation for paying too much for acquisitions and its depressed net earnings flow.

They were concerned whether STET, faced with the high level of Italian corporate taxes, can afford to keep its costs high, investments high and overpay for acquisitions to keep depreciation charges high. This depresses profits and so, keeps the tax charge low.
The resulting lower earnings makes comparisons with other telecoms groups difficult, they said.
Other analysts were concerned the share price has run ahead of itself before privatisation this autumn, which could result in a large stock offering.
STET's aggressive business plan, announced earlier this month, its winning bid for Spain's second telecoms group Retevision in June and its link with U.S. giant AT&T have boosted STET shares.

Earlier this month, STET announced the long-awaited link up with the AT&T-Unisource telecoms venture with an option of taking a 30-percent stake in the venture. Unisource contains Dutch, Swedish and Swiss telecoms partners.
Analysts said this link-up will strengthen STET's position in Europe and Latin America.

But one analyst said "there's a lot of euphoria in Italy over STET's share price. While some of this is justified, there are doubts over how useful the AT&T link up will be and on STET's future earnings performance."

Some also noted STET's link came after the British Telecom /MCI Communications Corp partnership had formed an alliance with Spain's main telecoms operator Telefonica to produce Concery and Sprint Corp , France Telecom and Deutsche Telekom formed Global One. ($ = 1742 Italian Lire)
